lines.text: On day twelve, all that stands between a bus and a kid is ten seconds.
lines.say: [low, slow] On day twelve, all that stands between a bus and a kid is ten seconds.

lines.text: But on day one, you just wake up and discover you can pause time.
lines.say: But on day one, you just wake up and discover you can pause time.

lines.text: The alarm's frozen mid-ring. Your cat's stuck halfway off the bed.
lines.say: The alarm's frozen mid-ring. Your cat's stuck halfway off the bed.

lines.text: So what if you could pause time for ten seconds a day?
lines.say: So what if you could pause time for ten seconds a day?

lines.text: Ten seconds. Once a day. Everyone and everything stops. Except you.
lines.say: Ten seconds. Once a day. Everyone and everything stops. Except you.

lines.text: When the ten run out, the world starts again, and nobody knows.
lines.say: When the ten run out, the world starts again, and nobody knows.

lines.text: And unused seconds vanish at midnight.
lines.say: And unused seconds vanish at midnight.

lines.text: So we cheat. Air moves for you. You can see. And anything you touch moves with you, then stops dead when you let go.
lines.say: So we cheat. Air moves for you. You can see. And anything you touch moves with you, then stops dead when you let go.

lines.text: So, what's your first pause for?
lines.say: So, what's your first pause for?

lines.text: Something selfish. Obviously.
lines.say: [dry] Something selfish. Obviously.

lines.text: A phone falls a metre in about 0.45 seconds. Usually, you just watch it go.
lines.say: A phone falls a metre in about nought point four five seconds. Usually, you just watch it go.

lines.text: Not today.
lines.say: Not today.

lines.text: You stroll over. There's no rush. At an ordinary walking pace, ten seconds covers about 10 to 14 metres.
lines.say: You stroll over. There's no rush. At an ordinary walking pace, ten seconds covers about ten to fourteen metres.

lines.text: Not a crack.
lines.say: Not a crack.

lines.text: Your boss spots you in the hallway. Stop and chat, or vanish?
lines.say: Your boss spots you in the hallway. Stop and chat, or vanish?

lines.text: Vanish.
lines.say: [dry] Vanish.

lines.text: The last samosa. A colleague's hand is already reaching. Do you let it go?
lines.say: The last samosa. A colleague's hand is already reaching. Do you let it go?

lines.text: Of course not. You're not a saint. You're a person with ten seconds.
lines.say: Of course not. You're not a saint. You're a person with ten seconds.

lines.text: Your mother's chappal, mid-air, aimed at your head? You step aside. She never works out how she missed.
lines.say: Your mother's chappal, mid-air, aimed at your head? You step aside. She never works out how she missed.

lines.text: Have you ever glanced at a clock and the second hand seemed to stick for a moment?
lines.say: Have you ever glanced at a clock and the second hand seemed to stick for a moment?

lines.text: That's real. Scientists call it chronostasis.
lines.say: That's real. Scientists call it chronostasis.

lines.text: Your brain has been editing time for you all your life. Now you've got the remote.
lines.say: Your brain has been editing time for you all your life. Now you've got the remote.

lines.text: Then comes day twelve. You're walking home.
lines.say: Then comes day twelve. You're walking home.

lines.text: A bus runs a red light.
lines.say: A bus runs a red light.

lines.text: There's a kid in the road.
lines.say: [sharp] There's a kid in the road.

lines.text: A car at 48 kilometres an hour needs about 23 metres to stop. And this is a bus.
lines.say: A car at forty-eight kilometres an hour needs about twenty-three metres to stop. [deadpan] And this is a bus.

lines.text: Do you shout? Do you run?
lines.say: Do you shout? Do you run?

lines.text: Neither works. Not in time.
lines.say: Neither works. Not in time.

lines.text: You hit pause.
lines.say: [quietly] You hit pause.

lines.text: You run.
lines.say: You run.

lines.text: Nine. Eight. Seven.
lines.say: [breathless] Nine. Eight. Seven.

lines.text: Six. Five. Four.
lines.say: [breathless] Six. Five. Four.

lines.text: Three. Two. One.
lines.say: [breathless] Three. Two. One.

lines.text: The bus screams through an empty crossing. The ball doesn't make it. The kid does.
lines.say: The bus screams through an empty crossing. The ball doesn't make it. The kid does.

lines.text: The kid's mother runs over, shaking. She thanks the bus driver. Nobody thanks you. Nobody knows to.
lines.say: The kid's mother runs over, shaking. She thanks the bus driver. Nobody thanks you. Nobody knows to.

lines.text: You saved a life with ten seconds. That feels free.
lines.say: You saved a life with ten seconds. That feels free.

lines.text: It is not free.
lines.say: [low] It is not free.

lines.text: Your body keeps ageing through every pause. Ten seconds a day that nobody else lives.
lines.say: Your body keeps ageing through every pause. Ten seconds a day that nobody else lives.

lines.text: And now you know what ten seconds can do. So you can't stop watching.
lines.say: And now you know what ten seconds can do. So you can't stop watching.

lines.text: One morning you're late, and the bus doors are closing. Catch it, or keep your seconds?
lines.say: One morning you're late, and the bus doors are closing. Catch it, or keep your seconds?

lines.text: Just this once.
lines.say: Just this once.

lines.text: That evening, your mother misses a step on the stairs. You snap your fingers. Nothing.
lines.say: That evening, your mother misses a step on the stairs. You snap your fingers. Nothing.

lines.text: She's all right. Bruised. You're not.
lines.say: [quietly] She's all right. Bruised. [pause] You're not.

lines.text: That night, you lie awake doing the maths of every second you've ever wasted.
lines.say: That night, you lie awake doing the maths of every second you've ever wasted.

lines.text: You almost never spend them on yourself again.
lines.say: You almost never spend them on yourself again.

lines.text: Some days nothing happens. So at midnight you spend them on nothing at all.
lines.say: Some days nothing happens. So at midnight you spend them on nothing at all.

lines.text: Ten seconds of a city holding its breath, just for you.
lines.say: [hushed] Ten seconds of a city holding its breath, just for you.

lines.text: Except, across the street, a curtain moves. In a window that should be frozen.
lines.say: Except, across the street, a curtain moves. In a window that should be frozen.

lines.text: The curtain never moves again. But every midnight, you check.
lines.say: The curtain never moves again. But every midnight, you check.

lines.text: Catch the six that wins your lane's cricket match? That, you do. Just the once.
lines.say: Catch the six that wins your lane's cricket match? That, you do. Just the once.

lines.text: Ten seconds is too small for greed. It's exactly the right size for an accident.
lines.say: Ten seconds is too small for greed. It's exactly the right size for an accident.

lines.text: You become the reason small disasters don't happen.
lines.say: You become the reason small disasters don't happen.

lines.text: Your mother asks you to stop waiting at the bottom of the stairs.
lines.say: Your mother asks you to stop waiting at the bottom of the stairs.

lines.text: Promise her, or keep watching?
lines.say: Promise her, or keep watching?

lines.text: You stay on the bottom step.
lines.say: You stay on the bottom step.

lines.text: Forty years in, you read a street like a weather map.
lines.say: Forty years in, you read a street like a weather map.

lines.text: You see the accident before it happens. Most days, you don't even need the pause.
lines.say: You see the accident before it happens. Most days, you don't even need the pause.

lines.text: Your body lives every one of those pauses. Over fifty years, they add up to about two days.
lines.say: Your body lives every one of those pauses. Over fifty years, they add up to about two days.

lines.text: That's how much older you are than everyone you grew up with. You'd barely notice.
lines.say: That's how much older you are than everyone you grew up with. You'd barely notice.

lines.text: The bigger cost is the watching. A whole life spent ten seconds at a time, on strangers who'll never know your name.
lines.say: The bigger cost is the watching. A whole life spent ten seconds at a time, on strangers who'll never know your name.

lines.text: And then you notice something.
lines.say: And then you notice something.

lines.text: Someone else is still moving.
lines.say: [hushed] Someone else is still moving.

lines.text: And they're looking right at you.
lines.say: [hushed] And they're looking right at you.

lines.text: Somebody knows.
lines.say: [whispers] Somebody knows.

lines.text: So what would you spend your ten seconds on? Tell us below. The best what-ifs become videos.
lines.say: So what would you spend your ten seconds on? Tell us below. The best what-ifs become videos.
